top_choice_rationale: Base editing (Liu, Komor, Gaudelli) is a clear, quantitatively demonstrated principle: an engineered deaminase on a nickase Cas9 converts one base in place without a double-strand break, with the evolved adenine editor as the genuinely new chemistry. It created a capability that did not exist, has been reproduced in very many laboratories for about ten years, and can be explained to a broad audience in one sentence. The costs, proximity to the 2020 CRISPR prize and the Target-AID attribution, are real but are outweighed by novelty and clarity. Targeted degradation (P001) is second as chemically new but harder to cite as one achievement, and C-N coupling (P002) third as mature but closer to the 2010 prize.
